description: July 8, 2016. Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani — 22 years old, the social-media face of the new Kashmiri insurgency — is killed in an encounter in Kokernag, Tral. His death triggers the worst Kashmir unrest since 2010: 90+ civilian deaths, 15,000+ pellet gun injuries over 7 months, 100+ youths joining militancy within weeks. Intelligence gathering in Kashmir suffers a 'temporary blow' as sources dry up amid community backlash. Rizwan Shah, monitoring the radicalisation pipeline from his position embedded in the ISI-linked Kashmiri network, must assess: is this a spontaneous grief surge or is ISI exploiting Wani's martyrdom to systematically recruit a new generation of militants before the political window closes?

real_world_correlation.real_event: Burhan Wani killed in encounter at Kokernag, Anantnag district, J&K. Security forces: 3 HM militants killed, 0 casualties. Wani's funeral attended by tens of thousands. Unrest lasted 7 months: 90 civilians killed, 15,000+ pellet gun injuries (1,000+ suffered partial or full blindness). Curfew in Kashmir Valley for weeks.
real_world_correlation.intelligence_collapse: India Today reported intelligence gathering in Kashmir 'suffered a temporary blow' after Wani's killing. Sources became unavailable; informer networks dried up as community sentiment turned against security forces. At least 100 youths joined militancy in the months post-Wani — a surge not seen since 2000.
real_world_correlation.isi_exploitation: ISI exploited the Wani narrative to rebrand Kashmiri militancy for a social-media era. Wani had never been involved in civilian killings — his clean image made him the ideal martyr. ISI's media operations used his death to recruit in madrassas, colleges, and via encrypted apps. TRF (The Resistance Front) — later responsible for Pahalgam — traces its ideological DNA to the post-Wani radicalisation cohort.
real_world_correlation.pellet_gun_controversy: The security forces' use of pellet guns as crowd control created global human rights condemnation and strengthened ISI's propaganda narrative. UN Human Rights Council cited J&K in 2018 report. Wani's death + pellet gun footage was weaponised internationally.
real_world_correlation.wani_social_media_doctrine: Wani pioneered the use of YouTube, WhatsApp, and Facebook by Kashmiri militants — bypassing traditional ISI-Hurriyat communication chains and speaking directly to Kashmiri youth. His death created a template for decentralised, leaderless radicalisation that Indian intelligence had not modelled.

mission_tasks.name: Assess whether ISI is directing Wani martyrdom exploitation or riding spontaneous grief
Map new militant recruitment pipeline — madrassa, college, encrypted app channels post-Wani
Identify radicalized youth cell leaders who will form next-generation militant organizations (TRF precursors)
Rebuild Kashmir intelligence source network after post-Wani community backlash dried up informers

adversaries.objective: Convert Wani martyrdom into systematic recruitment surge; rebrand militancy as legitimate resistance for international audience; exploit pellet gun controversy for propaganda; seed TRF-precursor cells before Indian intelligence rebuilds sources
Leverage unrest for political bargaining; coordinate with ISI without being directly implicated; present as civil society voice internationally

intelligence_targets.name: Confirmation that ISI is directing — not merely exploiting — post-Wani recruitment surge through specific operational channels
Identities of radicalised youth cell leaders who will form next-generation militant orgs (proto-TRF, 2019-onward)
Extent and coordination of ISI media operations weaponising pellet gun imagery internationally
